blogs.title: Beyond Type 1 and Type 2: How to Spot HNF1A‑MODY in a Young Adult
blogs.description: Walk clinicians through a step‑by‑step diagnostic algorithm for early‑onset diabetes that doesn’t fit classic type 1 or type 2 patterns. Highlight red flags – strong autosomal dominant family history, negative pancreatic autoantibodies, borderline C‑peptide, pronounced post‑prandial spikes and unexplained glycosuria – and discuss how tools like the Exeter MODY probability calculator perform across ethnicities. Emphasize when genetic testing should be ordered and common pitfalls that lead to misdiagnosis.

blogs.title: A New HNF1A Variant (p.N270S) from Taiwan: Interpreting Novel Mutations with ACMG Guidelines
blogs.description: Explore the discovery of the heterozygous p.N270S substitution in exon 4 of HNF1A and walk through modern variant interpretation using ACMG/AMP criteria. Cover population frequency checks, computational scores (AlphaMissense), segregation data within families, domain relevance (DNA‑binding domain), and the limits of public databases such as ClinVar. Provide a practical framework for clinicians faced with an “unreported” variant and discuss how expanding variant catalogs affect precision care across diverse populations.

blogs.title: Rethinking First‑Line Therapy: GLP‑1 Receptor Agonists Versus Sulfonylureas in HNF1A‑MODY
blogs.description: Compare historical low‑dose sulfonylurea treatment with newer GLP‑1 receptor agonist strategies for HNF1A‑MODY. Summarize evidence from crossover trials and the presented case where dulaglutide enabled insulin discontinuation and drove HbA₁c from 10 % to 6 % within months. Discuss mechanisms (β‑cell sensitisation vs insulin secretion), hypoglycaemia risk, weight impact, durability as β‑cell function declines, and practical algorithms for transitioning patients after genetic confirmation.

blogs.title: When Glycosuria Isn’t Just Hyperglycaemia: The Hidden Dangers of SGLT2 Inhibitors in HNF1A‑MODY
blogs.description: Explain why patients with HNF1A mutations have a reduced renal glucose threshold due to impaired SGLT2 transcription. Review case reports linking SGLT2 inhibition to severe dehydration, euglycaemic ketoacidosis, and vascular collapse in this subgroup. Offer safety checks before prescribing SGLT2 inhibitors – assessing renal threshold, monitoring hydration status, and considering alternative agents – so clinicians can avoid iatrogenic complications.

blogs.title: NGS Panels for Early‑Onset Diabetes: From Cost Containment to Precision Care
blogs.description: Detail how next‑generation sequencing panels have transformed MODY screening. Present prevalence data from Asian cohorts, diagnostic yield versus selective testing based on clinical criteria, and cost–benefit analyses showing savings from avoiding unnecessary insulin or sulfonylurea use. Discuss workflow for ordering panels, interpretation turnaround, cascade testing of relatives, insurance considerations, and future directions such as whole exome/genome approaches.
